profiles/chemical/canonical-smiles/v0.1..compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target requires is satisfied. Missing required information returns UNKNOWN. Every conversion or inference must be declared and versioned.
profiles/chemical/canonical-smiles/v0.1..description: A SMILES representation designated canonical by a declared canonicalization method, software implementation and version for a specified chemical structure.

examples.conditions: Both ports declare different methods and no normalising adapter is supplied.
examples.title: Different canonicalization methods are incompatible
examples.why: Canonical SMILES is method-dependent, so different declared methods cannot be assumed identical.

examples.conditions: The source omits the tool version required by the target contract.
examples.title: Missing canonicalization tool version is unknown
examples.why: The same tool can change canonical output between versions.

examples.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
examples.title: Identical canonical-SMILES contracts are exact matches
examples.why: The same complete canonical-SMILES declaration can connect without conversion or approval.

profiles/chemical/canonical-smiles/v0.1..intended_use: Connecting a model output that provides canonical SMILES to a model input that expects the same declared canonicalization method and software version.
profiles/chemical/canonical-smiles/v0.1..label: Canonical SMILES
limitations: It does not establish that two differently normalised strings represent the same chemical entity.
It does not silently resolve stereochemistry, protonation, tautomer, isotope or charge choices.
profiles/chemical/canonical-smiles/v0.1..name: canonical-smiles
profiles/chemical/canonical-smiles/v0.1..scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It does not show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.

sources.title: SMILES, a Chemical Language and Information System. 1. Introduction to Methodology and Encoding Rules

profiles/proteome/protein-sequence/v0.1..compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target requires is satisfied. Missing required information returns UNKNOWN. Every conversion or inference must be declared and versioned.
profiles/proteome/protein-sequence/v0.1..description: An amino-acid residue sequence representing a declared protein or polypeptide, with the identifier namespace, namespace version and organism context needed to interpret it.

examples.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
examples.title: Identical protein-sequence contracts are exact matches
examples.why: The same complete sequence declaration can connect without conversion or approval.

examples.conditions: Both ports declare different alphabets and no translation step is supplied.
examples.title: Different sequence alphabets are incompatible
examples.why: Amino-acid and nucleotide strings do not have the same biological interpretation.

examples.conditions: The source omits the encoding required by the target contract.
examples.title: Missing sequence encoding is unknown
examples.why: The sequence cannot be interpreted reliably when its encoding is not declared.

profiles/proteome/protein-sequence/v0.1..intended_use: Connecting a model output that provides an amino-acid sequence to a model input that consumes a protein or polypeptide sequence.
profiles/proteome/protein-sequence/v0.1..label: Protein Sequence
limitations: It does not cover nucleotide sequences or establish that a sequence is scientifically correct.
It does not justify cross-species substitution or an undeclared change of sequence encoding.
profiles/proteome/protein-sequence/v0.1..name: protein-sequence
profiles/proteome/protein-sequence/v0.1..scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It does not show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.

profiles/proteome/protein-structure/v0.1.compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target requires is satisfied. Missing required information returns UNKNOWN. Every conversion or inference must be declared and versioned.
profiles/proteome/protein-structure/v0.1.description: A three-dimensional structural representation of a declared protein or protein-containing assembly, including the identity, coordinate representation and format needed to interpret the structure.

examples.conditions: Both ports declare different coordinate systems and no conversion is supplied.
examples.title: Different coordinate systems are incompatible
examples.why: Coordinates in different systems cannot be consumed as if their numerical values have the same spatial meaning.

examples.conditions: The source omits the structure origin required by the target contract.
examples.title: Missing structure origin is unknown
examples.why: Experimental, predicted and otherwise derived structures have different provenance and limitations.

examples.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
examples.title: Identical protein-structure contracts are exact matches
examples.why: The same complete structure declaration can connect without conversion or approval.

profiles/proteome/protein-structure/v0.1.intended_use: Connecting a model output that provides a three-dimensional protein structure to a model input that consumes the same declared structural representation.
profiles/proteome/protein-structure/v0.1.label: Protein Structure
limitations: It does not establish structural accuracy, biological function or fitness for a downstream claim.
A predicted structure is not treated as interchangeable with an experimental structure unless the target permits that origin.
profiles/proteome/protein-structure/v0.1.name: protein-structure
profiles/proteome/protein-structure/v0.1.scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It does not show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.

rules/units.json.alias_note: Informal spellings that UCUM does not define are unsupported; use the UCUM spelling.
rules/units.json.note: Every unit resolved to a factor over the UCUM base units, a dimension vector in the order given by 'dimensions', and for affine units an offset such that base_value = factor * value + offset. Units flagged arbitrary are not commensurable with anything else, per UCUM section 24, so they convert only to themselves. Units UCUM defines through logarithmic or other non-affine functions are listed in 'unresolved' and must never be converted silently.
